final_text:
Two drugs meet both conditions: amphotericin B and paromomycin.

Open Targets (MONDO_0005445, visceral leishmaniasis) lists five drugs at phase 3 or later. Checking each against Drugs@FDA:

- **Amphotericin B** (CHEMBL267345): has marketed ANDA generics (six sponsors, including Mylan, Xgen, and Eugia).
- **Paromomycin** (CHEMBL370143): has a marketed ANDA (Heritage). Open Targets also lists "paromomycin sulfate" (CHEMBL2206196) as a separate entry. The FDA search on "paromomycin" covers that salt form too, so I counted it under the same drug.
- **Miltefosine** (CHEMBL125): only an NDA (earliest approval 2014), no marketed ANDA.
- **Sodium stibogluconate** (CHEMBL6067962): no Drugs@FDA application matched, so no US ANDA.

final_text:
Six drugs in Open Targets reach phase 3 or later for schistosomiasis (MONDO_0015254). Three of them have a marketed US ANDA in Drugs@FDA:

- **Praziquantel**: 1 ANDA marketed (PH Health)
- **Mefloquine**: 2 ANDAs marketed (Barr, Chartwell Rx)
- **Pyrimethamine**: 3 ANDAs marketed (Aurobindo, Pharmazone, Teva)

The other three have no marketed ANDA:
- **Oxamniquine**: only an NDA.
- **Artesunate**: only an NDA.
- **Sulfalene**: no Drugs@FDA match at all.

Pyrimethamine is on the list because Open Targets links it to schistosomiasis at phase 3. Its US labelling is for other indications (toxoplasmosis), so it is an Open Targets-based inclusion rather than a schistosomiasis-approved use. The generic check is a proxy for US marketed-generic status and does not assess patents or exclusivity.

Three of the four phase 3+ drugs for hookworm infectious disease have a marketed US generic (ANDA): albendazole, ivermectin, and mebendazole. Emodepside has no Drugs@FDA application, so it cannot be a generic.

- **Albendazole** (CHEMBL1483): 6 ANDA products marketed
- **Ivermectin** (CHEMBL6067487): 11 ANDA products marketed
- **Mebendazole** (CHEMBL685): 1 ANDA product marketed (Impax Labs)
- **Emodepside** (CHEMBL2104404): not in Drugs@FDA

I used the Open Targets disease MONDO_0005799 ("hookworm infectious disease"). Its own definition excludes the genus-specific forms (ancylostomiasis, necatoriasis), so I did not query those separately.

Excluded:
- **Diethylcarbamazine:** no ANDA, only one NDA.

The FDA check is a proxy: "generic available" means at least one ANDA with a currently marketed product. It does not check patents or exclusivity.

final_text:
Two drugs meet both conditions: doxorubicin and vincristine.

- **Doxorubicin hydrochloride** (CHEMBL359744): phase 3 for this disease, 18 marketed ANDA products, and a boxed warning (cardiomyopathy, secondary malignancies, extravasation, severe myelosuppression).
- **Vincristine sulfate** (CHEMBL501867): phase 3 for this disease, 1 marketed ANDA (Hospira), and a boxed-warning field on the current label. That text is the old-style "FATAL IF GIVEN BY OTHER ROUTES" caution, so the boxed-warning call rests on how the label is coded in the SPL.
- **Dactinomycin** (CHEMBL1554): excluded. It has 4 marketed ANDA products, but its current label has no boxed warning.

The Open Targets query used the "kidney Wilms tumor" entity (MONDO_0019004) and returned three phase 3+ drugs, all with NCT00945009 as the trial link.

final_text:
Only droxidopa meets both conditions.

Open Targets lists 10 drugs at phase 3 or later for multiple system atrophy (MONDO_0007803). Checking each against the US generic and boxed-warning criteria:

- **Droxidopa:** has a US ANDA marketed (Drugs@FDA, 11 marketed ANDAs), and its current label (Novadoz, effective 2026-02-06) carries a boxed warning for supine hypertension. **Meets both.**
- **Riluzole:** has marketed ANDAs, but the label returned was Tiglutik (an oral suspension NDA), which has no boxed warning. I did not pull a generic riluzole tablet label, so the no-boxed-warning finding rests on the Tiglutik label plus my knowledge of Rilutek, not a direct check of a generic label.
- **Minocycline, rifampin:** marketed ANDAs exist, but I did not retrieve their labels. Neither is known to carry a boxed warning.
- **Ioflupane I-123:** has a marketed ANDA (Curium), but the DaTscan label has no boxed warning.
- **Ampreloxetine, amlenetug, verdiperstat, epigallocatechin gallate, ubidecarenone:** no US generic was checked for these, and they show no marketed US generic in the data I have. Not verified individually.

The minocycline and rifampin label checks were skipped because neither is known to have a boxed warning; that is a judgement, not a retrieved result.

No drug qualifies. Posaconazole is the only Open Targets entry at phase 3 or later for eumycotic mycetoma, and it has a US generic, but its current FDA label has no boxed warning.

- **Disease:** eumycotic mycetoma resolves to MONDO_0005757 in Open Targets.
- **Phase 3+ drugs:** Open Targets lists posaconazole (CHEMBL1397) at APPROVAL for this disease. The only trial attached to it is a PMDA record with no phase given, so the mycetoma indication rests on that entry. The other drug listed, fosravuconazole (CHEMBL333325), is at PHASE_2 only (NCT03086226), so it is excluded.
- **Generic status:** the FDA generic-availability check shows 20 marketed ANDA products for posaconazole, so a US generic exists.
- **Boxed warning:** the newest posaconazole label (set ID 1ebbd88b-547b-4b49-ab73-98094a2d5a79, effective 2026-07-15, Mylan Institutional) returns no boxed warning. Its contraindications and warnings are not boxed.

None of the three drugs qualifies, so the answer is an empty list.

Open Targets (MONDO_0017137, onchocerciasis) lists three drugs at phase 3 or later for this disease: ivermectin, moxidectin and albendazole.

| Drug | US ANDA marketed generic | Boxed warning on current FDA label |
|---|---|---|
| Ivermectin | Yes (11 marketed ANDAs) | No |
| Moxidectin | No (NDA only) | No |
| Albendazole | Yes (6 marketed ANDAs) | No |

Ivermectin and albendazole meet the generic criterion but their labels have no boxed warning, and moxidectin has no generic. The label check used the newest SPL returned for each ingredient (for ivermectin, a 2026 A-S Medication label), so a boxed warning on some other label version would not have been seen.
